descriptionChirho: A female offspring or descendant, used both literally (of a biological daughter) and in extended address or descent formulas (e.g., 'daughter of Zion', 'daughters of Jerusalem'). All three clusters represent inflectional variants: singular forms across all cases (S69297), plural forms (S69298), and a genitive singular (S69300) which is simply part of the singular paradigm. Translations are uniform: 'daughter(s)' (eng), 'hija(s)' (spa), 'binti' (swa), 'beti/betiyon' (hin), 'ibnat/banaat' (arb), 'ttal/ttaldeul' (kor). No semantic distinction warrants separate senses.
